question: Can token n-grams index a small, context-conditioned memory of expert responses, reducing weight reads even when weights are resident?
scope: Offline local expert-response interpolation; no approximate model generation, no speed claim.
data: Three distinct natural greedy continuations: code, explanation, reasoning; up to 512 generated tokens each. Existing short traces are exploratory only.
reference: Full grouped GPU expert replay on accepted full-model inputs. Discard speculative tails. Count repeated controls separately.
calibration: First 128 accepted decode input positions, including the last prompt position; frozen memory for the remaining positions. This does not capture prefill expert activations.
memory_cap: 16 most recent calibration exemplars per key; keep x and full GPU y. No held-out outputs used for lookup, prediction or updates.
methods: nearest input and its cached output
affine response interpolation on up to 16 cached input/output pairs, ridge 0.001 of mean Gram diagonal, reject coefficient L1 > 4
guards: Relative input residual <= 1%, 3%, 5%, 10%; unguarded coverage/error also reported. Guard reads current x, not current expert output.
metrics: routed local relative L2 mean/P99/max with full fallback
compact-memory bytes and descriptor traffic estimates
screen: Exploratory engineering screen: mean routed relative L2 <=3%, P99<=10%, ideal all-tier routed weight saving >=3%, independently on all three texts. Not a guarantee of answer quality; any selected policy needs fresh holdout and online tests.
controls: accepted position and token identity against generated stream
all protected Daily files unchanged; owned engines exited
limitations: Short contexts and four layers; finite sample. No inference that n-grams predict hidden states exactly. Nonlinear expert-output interpolation is approximate and differs from exact per-linear-layer Wb reuse. KV262144 is capacity, not tested depth. No trained Engram changes.
